tips.title: Choosing the Right Cement for ABS vs Polystyrene
tips.text: Tamiya Extra Thin Cement bonds polystyrene perfectly by melting the plastic together, but it struggles with ABS parts found in many modern kits (breeches, gun barrels, ICM and Arma Hobby aircraft propellers). For ABS, switch to Tamiya ABS & Polystyrene Cement in the green bottle, which contains ABS-compatible solvents. Apply sparingly with a fine brush to both surfaces, press together for 10 seconds, and let cure for 24 hours before sanding. Test the bond on a spare sprue first.

tips.title: Selecting Paint Type: Acrylic vs Enamel vs Lacquer
tips.text: For most scale models, acrylics like Vallejo Acrylic Paints are versatile and easy to use. They're water-based, non-toxic, and offer a wide range of colors. Enamels like Tamiya Acrylic Paints are great for fine detail work due to their thin consistency but require a longer drying time. Lacquers like Alclad II provide a smooth, high-gloss finish ideal for clear parts but require specialized thinners and ventilation. Choose based on your model's requirements.

tips.title: Choosing Sandpaper Grits for Each Stage
tips.text: Start with 220-grit sandpaper for general use, smoothing out major imperfections. For filling gaps and seams, use 320-grit after applying filler. For preparing surfaces for paint, use 400-grit to remove any remaining imperfections. Fine-tune details with 500-grit before painting. Always sand in one direction to avoid creating scratches. Use wet sanding with water or appropriate lubricant for better control.

tips.title: Selecting Filler for Gaps: Tamiya Putty vs Vallejo Plastic Putty vs Super Glue + Baking Soda
tips.text: Tamiya Putty is ideal for filling large gaps and seams. Apply with a toothpick or brush, let dry, then gently scrape off excess with a razor blade. Vallejo Plastic Putty is softer and more suitable for fine gaps. Apply with a fine brush, let dry, then sand smooth. For small gaps, mix a few drops of super glue with baking soda until it forms a thick paste. Apply with a toothpick, let dry, then sand smooth.

tips.title: Photo-Etch vs Resin Detail Parts
tips.text: Photo-etch parts like those from Eduard offer exceptional detail but require careful bending and handling. Use Eduard's Photo-Etch Bending Tools to curve parts gently without breaking them. For large, complex details, resin parts from companies like MiniArt or Arma Hobby can be easier to handle but may require additional cleaning and preparation. Choose based on the size and complexity of the detail needed.
